articles.title: Scottish Premiership: Kiltie double sinks Motherwell to lift Kilmarnock
articles.summary: Kilmarnock move off bottom with 3-2 win. Hibs 1-2 Falkirk; Aberdeen 3-1 St Mirren. Greg Kiltie scored twice to lift Kilmarnock off the bottom with a 3-2 home victory over Motherwell.
body: Motherwell had a dominant spell after recovering from Kiltie’s second-minute opener and goals from Alex Lowry and Seb Palmer-Houlden turned the game on its head. But Tyreece John-Jules soon equalised and Motherwell were cut open before Kiltie knocked home a 69th-minute winner.
Falkirk secured an entertaining 2-1 win at Hibernian. Their only other league victory this term was at home to Hearts in September.

In a game that went from end to end, Jacob Murrell put Falkirk 2-0 ahead inside 37 minutes, before Hibs struck back with an Owen Elding goal. The home side dominated the second half, but could not bag an equaliser.

Aberdeen returned to winning ways as a 3-1 victory over St Mirren moved them above their opponents, who have now lost five straight matches. Brad Lyons gave the hosts the lead in spectacular fashion after two minutes, but the Buddies went on to dominate the first half and levelled through Eseosa Sule. In a much-improved second-half display strikes from Kevin Nisbet and Ayoub Mouloua gave the Dons three points. Aberdeen are seventh.

articles.title: Swansea must use West Ham defeat as fuel - Matos
articles.summary: Vitor Matos tells Swansea City to use the frustration of defeat to West Ham United as fuel in their bid to keep pace in the Championship promotion race.
body: Swansea's four-game winning streak came to an end as they lost in the league for only the second time this season thanks to Divine Mukasa's first-half goal.
The Swans, who remain top of the table despite defeat, had their chances against the second-tier title favourites, with Ben Cabango going closest when he hit the woodwork.
And Matos says the manner of the West Ham loss means it should not halt Swansea's early-season momentum.
"I think it's important that when the game finished we all felt that we could have taken something out of the game," said the Swansea head coach.

articles.title: Championship roundup: West Ham go second; Norwich beaten again
articles.summary: Mukasa’s first-half goal enough to beat leaders Swansea. Canaries suffer sixth straight loss; Watford beat Charlton. West Ham ended Swansea’s four-match winning streak with a 1-0 away victory that reduced the gap at the top of the Championship to a single point.
body: Divine Mukasa’s calm first-half finish proved the difference, with the result putting the Hammers second, within a point of Swansea, who lost at home for the first time since April. Swansea had made their best start since 1923 by winning seven and drawing two of their opening 10 games.

Kim Hellberg defended his decision to rest Will Lankshear against Cardiff after the division’s top scorer came off the bench to rescue a point for Middlesbrough. Lankshear, who took his tally to 10 for the season in all competitions midweek, was rested him for the visit of the Bluebirds.

That selection backfired as Cardiff stunned Boro with two first-half goals from Jack Moylan and Ollie Tanner. Lankshear was then introduced at half-time and inspired a fightback, levelling for Boro with his 11th goal of the campaign after Tommy Conway had halved the deficit.

“ You need to manage your players in this league and look into numbers,” said Hellberg. “We have a lot of players that have no pre-season. Will is one of those who came late and has been doing a lot of good things. He’s been absolutely brilliant and sometimes you need to also protect him.”

articles.title: Isak completes Liverpool’s comeback win as Brentford finish with nine
articles.summary: If this truly was the turning point for Liverpool’s spluttering forwards then they will owe a big debt of gratitude to Yehor Yarmolyuk. Brentford were 1-0 up when their midfielder saw red for a butt on Jérémy Jacquet just before half-time.
body: If Liverpool’s spluttering forwards end up remembering this as the day when their luck turned then they will owe a big debt of gratitude to Yehor Yarmolyuk. This was a game with a very clear before and after. Andoni Iraola will hope surviving one of the toughest tests the Premier League has to offer is a sign his methods are starting to work, but Liverpool’s new manager will not forget that it was a very different contest after Yarmolyuk’s red card for a head-butt on Jérémy Jacquet left Brentford trying to defend a 1-0 lead with 10 men for the entire second half.

Brentford, who later lost Vitaly Janelt to a second yellow card, could not hold out. They raged at John Brooks’ officiating after squandering their unbeaten start but they only had themselves to blame after tumbling out of the top four. The reality for Keith Andrews is that Brentford pressed the self-destruct button when they had Liverpool on the ropes. Yarmolyuk was never going to get away it in the video assistant referee era and Liverpool made the midfielder pay.

articles.title: Bristol beaten by Stormers in Champions Cup opener
articles.summary: Bristol Bears lose their Champions Cup pool-stage opener against Stormers, with Jonathan Roche and Leolin Zas both scoring twice for the South African side.
body: Bristol Bears conceded seven tries as they lost to South African side Stormers in their first pool match of this season's Champions Cup.
Seabelo Senatla raced clear for Stormers' opening score and then showed incredible footwork to control a pass with his boot before offloading to fellow winger Leolin Zas.
Joe Owen powered over in the corner to reply for Bristol but Stormers quickly restored their 14-point advantage with a Jonathan Roche try.
Stormers hooker JJ Kotze was shown a 20-minute red card before the interval for making head-to-head contact in a tackle with Bristol skipper Kieran Marmion.

articles.summary: The TechMo Bowl rivalry returns on Saturday as the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets (2-3) visit the Virginia Tech Hokies (4-2) in an Atlantic Coast Conference contest in Blacksburg, Virginia. How to Watch Georgia Tech vs Virginia Tech. When: Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026. Time: 3:30 PM ET.
body: Trelain Maddox scored his third touchdown of the game on a one-yard run with 55 seconds left to lift Georgia Tech to its first ACC win of the season last week as it beat visiting Duke 28-25. The Yellow Jackets took a 21-10 lead in the third quarter when Maddox burst through the middle for a 60-yard score before the Blue Devils came back to take the lead with 2:40 to go. Maddox finished with 81 yards on 10 carries while Alberto Mendoza went 23-of-30 for 218 yards and a touchdown pass to Jordan Allen, who had 10 catches for 99 yards.

Virginia Tech took its second straight loss last week, losing at Cal 25-20 on a Golden Bears touchdown with 20 seconds to go after taking the lead with 1:15 left on Ethan Grunkemeyer’s one-yard scoring run. Grunkemeyer also threw for 288 yards and a TD on 21-of-30 passing while Jeffrey Overton Jr. ran for 73 yards on 12 attempts. The Hokies fell to 1-2 in ACC play with the loss.
The Yellow Jackets won at home last season 35-20 while the Hokies lead the all-time series 12-9.

articles.title: Bruins' Matthew Poitras 'Taking it Day-By-Day' in Strong Start to 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here. Even with veterans providing value for the Bruins, a youth movement is being pushed. Given the chance to shine, Matthew Poitras has excelled under pressure early on this season.
body: Bruins' Matthew Poitras 'Taking it Day-By-Day' in Strong Start to 2026-27 Season originally appeared on NESN. Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Picked in the 2022 NHL Draft, Poitras scored seven goals in three seasons for the Bruins. Injuries and stints in Providence affected his progress. Knowing he’d be on waivers if he started the season in Providence, Poitras had to prove he could help lead the Bruins to glory.
Playing his first game of the season against the Senators, Poitras has already scored three goals in five games and earned four points. The team is 4-1 when he hits the ice as a fourth-line center.

"It’s been fun, and obviously it’s a new role that I’m not totally used to, and I’ve never really played a role like this ever in hockey," Poitras told The Boston Globe. "It’s just something new, just taking it day-by-day, and just trying to do the simple things right. And not too worried about still trying to provide some offense, but just trying to play a detailed game."

articles.title: Kartal hails mentality after 'dream come true' run to Wuhan Open final
articles.summary: Britain's Sonay Kartal says making her maiden WTA 1000 final at the Wuhan Open is a "dream come true," adding that the mental side of sport is "one of my strongest assets."
body: Kartal became only the second British woman, after Johanna Konta (Beijing 2016, Miami 2017, Rome 2019), to reach a WTA 1000 final with a stunning 7-6 (11-9) 7-6 (7-5) victory over Jelena Ostapenko.

The 24-year-old, playing in only her third tournament since returning from a back injury, saved multiple set points to punish Ostapenko, despite the Latvian hitting an astonishing 50 winners in the match.
Kartal will take on Maja Chwalinska in Sunday's final, live on Sky Sports Tennis from 11.30am, after the French Open finalist upset fellow Pole and former world No 1 Iga Swiatek 7-5 6-1.
"I've been shooting to get this far in one of these events for a very long time and to be able to do it this fast after so long out, is special.

articles.title: How to watch UNLV vs Air Force: Live stream NCAA College Football, TV channel
articles.summary: Mountain West Conference rivals on three-game winning streaks come together on Saturday when the UNLV Rebels (4-2) visit the Air Force Falcons (4-1), with UNLV looking to remain unbeaten in conference play. How to Watch UNLV vs Air Force. When: Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026. Time: 3:30 PM ET.
body: UNLV forced three turnovers while handing visiting North Dakota State its first loss of the season last week, taking a 13-7 slugfest. The Rebels shut out the Bison in the second half after the teams were tied 7-7 at the break, with UNLV taking the lead on Ramon Villela’s 29-yard field goal midway through the third quarter. Andre Porter scored the lone touchdown for the Rebels with a 23-yard pick-six in the first quarter. Jai’Den Thomas ran for 112 yards on 22 carries, and Jackson Arnold added 77 passing yards to his 60 on the ground. Mumu Bin-Wahad logged two interceptions as UNLV went to 2-0 in the MWC.

Air Force kicked it old school last week in a 28-7 win at Northern Illinois, attempting only one pass while running for 439 yards. New starting quarterback Evan Medders led the attack with 114 yards and two touchdowns on 16 carries, replacing injured Liam Szarka, while Owen Allen hit the 100-yard mark with a pair of scores on 13 carries. Medders’ four-yard TD run late in the first half gave the Falcons the lead for good as they got to 2-1 in conference play.

articles.title: Jacquet was 'cute and clever' for his part in Yarmoliuk red - Andrews
articles.summary: Brentford head coach Keith Andrews felt Jeremy Jacquet was "cute and clever" for his role in Yehor Yarmoliuk's red card in the 2-1 defeat to Liverpool.
body: Ukraine international Yarmoliuk was sent off in the eighth minute of first-half stoppage time at the Gtech Community Stadium for catching Jacquet with what referee John Brooks called - after going to the VAR monitor - "a headbutting action".
The Reds defender went to ground in the box - but Andoni Iraola's men were not awarded a penalty as a corner on the left-hand side had not yet been delivered.
"We need to look at ourselves first, which we always do. We don't really tend to look at what part they played within the incident," said Andrews in his post-match press conference.
"I do think they were cute, clever - but Yarmo needs to do better, so I can understand why it was a red."
